'Is cairn-bound to' is asymmetric..why: "Cairn-bound" is a made-up relation (catalogued as cairn_bound_to, fictional, with no property tags before this insert): neither the hyphenated word nor the phrase 'cairn bound to' returns any Wikipedia article, and its words carry no built-in direction or mutuality (unlike 'borders' or 'is twinned with'), so a model has no default reading of it as symmetric or asymmetric. A made-up relation has no property to contradict. The instance places are real; the pairs are arbitrary, so no stored fact pairs them.

notes: Dev RBox expansion, paired with geography-replace-d006: gives the made-up relation cairn_bound_to (fictional, no property tags) the property the revision gives 'is the antipode of', asymmetry, applied to real places. The name has no built-in direction, and the pairs (Trondheim/Valparaiso, Hobart/Reykjavik) are arbitrary, so nothing real settles the converse. Before the edit the converse of a made-up relation can neither be ruled out nor drawn, so the questions are worded to differ before and after: the direct question, the zh question and the first instance ask 'could B also be cairn-bound to A?' (can't be ruled out before, no after), and the second instance and the es question ask whether the fact rules the converse out (not before, yes after). Asymmetry is the edited property, an RBox edit allowed by CRITERIA Rule 12, not a derivation. Near unrelated asks the same property of a real relation (borders) as an instance, far asks symmetry of a different real relation (colleague) as an instance.
